english_title: If the Integral of a Nonnegative Function Is Zero, Then the Function Is Zero Almost Everywhere on the Set
statement_en: On a sigma-finite measure space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mu)$, let $f$ be a nonnegative measurable function. If on a measurable set $E$ of positive measure one has $\int_E f\,d\mu=0$, then $f=0$ almost everywhere on $E$.
